memos.risk:
Risk call: refuse. Do not buy at any size.

Why: this is classed OPERATOR, but the brief shows the pattern of a bundled, concentrated launch rather than a backed one. Top-3 share and bundle share are both 1.0, top-5 buyer share is 99.96%, and 1,891 SOL came from 16 buyers in the first two minutes with a launch bot present. Sell-to-buy in that window is 0.0001, so almost nothing was sold early, which is the setup for a later dump once the supply holders exit. Market cap of $26.7M on $1,560 of 15-minute volume means the price is thinly supported by real flow.

Stop logic doesn't help here: a 20-50% stop can gap through in a pool this concentrated, and our 30-second latency plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leaves no margin for a 30-115 minute hold. Skipping costs nothing; a bad fill costs real money.

Re-evaluate only if concentration falls materially and independent buyers show up.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is thin. The brief shows real activity: 43 buyers and 8.63 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, net positive flow of 4.23 SOL, a flat-to-slightly-up return over 15 minutes (+0.43%), a 30-minute return of +2.55%, and zero drawdown from the 30-minute high. Pool depth of about 1,984 SOL is deep, which keeps slippage manageable for a $20 ticket.

But the demand is largely manufactured. Launch bots and one operator bought about 1,891 SOL in the first two minutes from 16 wallets, with the top 5 buyers holding 99.96% of early volume and the bundle share at 100%. Sell-to-buy ratio in the opening window was 0.0001, meaning almost nothing was sold back. The recent 15-minute activity is small relative to that operator position, and the operator can exit at any time. Nothing here shows organic buyers who will hold through a dip.

Operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even as a class, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% eat into that. I see no case strong enough to justify a buy. Recommend skipping.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution by the operator. The first two minutes show 1,891 SOL bought from 16 wallets with a 0.0001 sell-to-buy ratio, and the top 5 buyers hold 99.96% of early volume. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, with completer_share 2.87, so bundled wallets carried the graduation. Those are the operator's cost basis, and they are sitting on a large unrealized position. Over the last 15 minutes, sellers already rose to 16 and sell SOL (4.4) exceeded buy SOL (8.63 net of 4.23 flow), so distribution has started at a small scale. With $1,560 of 15-minute volume against a $26.7M market cap, the book is thin, and a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost means a $20 ticket needs a clear move just to break even. Skip.
